method: Syllogism checked by enumerating set models
steps: Some shirts are pants; pants ⊂ jackets ⊂ trousers.
A shirt that is a pant is a trouser -> Some trousers are shirts (I) always true.
II (All jackets are shirts) fails in a model where some jacket is not a shirt.
Only I follows.
check_code:
from itertools import product
# 4 sets over up to 5 elements; each element = membership tuple (Sh,P,J,T)
types=[t for t in product([0,1],repeat=4)]
I_always=True; II_always=True; found=False
for combo in product([0,1],repeat=len(types)):
    els=[t for t,c in zip(types,combo) if c]
    if not any(t[0] and t[1] for t in els): continue
    if any(t[1] and not t[2] for t in els): continue
    if any(t[2] and not t[3] for t in els): continue
    found=True
    I=any(t[3] and t[0] for t in els)
    II=all(t[0] for t in els if t[2])
    I_always&=I; II_always&=II
assert found
res={(True,False):'A',(False,True):'B',(True,True):'C',(False,False):'D'}[(I_always,II_always)]
assert res=='A' and res not in ('B','C','D')
